**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not enqueue rules for permission-filtered updates**

When a read-only account member PATCHes a transaction (or a read-write member submits only full-control fields), `permitted_entry_params` is `{}`, but `update({})` still succeeds; this unconditional call then invokes family-level rules although no authorized field changed. This lets that user trigger immediate actions such as AI calls or transfer creation on an account they cannot edit, so enqueue only after detecting an actual permitted change.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L8-L8](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/blob/61ec9f76a8dc272bb2a1bf85b33c49d13b8cca77/AGENTS.md#L8-L8)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply transaction IDs before resolving regex matches**

When an immediate run includes a `matches_regex` condition, this predicate is added only after `rule.matching_scope` returns; `Rule#matching_scope` eagerly executes `scope.pluck(:id)` under `SafeRegex` for regex conditions, so it has already scanned the rule's full family scope. On a large family, every one-row edit can consume the full timeout or create substantial repeated worker load even when the edited row is irrelevant; restrict the scope to these IDs before regex resolution.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wait for asynchronous rule actions before refreshing**

When an immediate rule uses `auto_categorize` or `auto_detect_merchants`, `Rule::Runner` leaves its run pending while a low-priority child job performs the work, but this condition broadcasts the sync toast immediately. `sync_toast_controller.js` auto-refreshes idle pages after two seconds, while `RuleRun#complete_job!` does not broadcast again, so users can refresh before the AI result exists and never be notified when it does; broadcast only after pending jobs drain and actually modify data.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**Pass only changed transaction IDs to immediate rules.**

When a mixed selection contains full-control and read-write transactions, a `name` or `date` update can change the full-control transactions while the read-write update removes those attributes. `Entry#bulk_update!` still reports the relation size, so `updated.positive?` enqueues every selected transaction ID.

`Rule::Runner` filters rules by the supplied IDs, not by transactions changed by this bulk edit. Matching read-write transactions can therefore execute immediate rule actions even though the bulk edit did not change them.

Collect the changed transaction IDs from both bulk-update partitions and pass only those IDs to `Rule.apply_immediately_later`.
